stage_a.note: She dances, smiles widely, and delivers with vibrant, sustained positive expression throughout.
She shows pronounced, sustained excitement about her culture, using big gestures and high energy.
She greets the panel cheerfully and maintains a friendly, approachable orientation during the pitch.

venture.description: Handwoven, colorful baskets and home decor items made by artisans in Senegal, sold directly to consumers online.
venture.note: She is seeking to expand into retail to lower customer acquisition costs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She introduces herself, her background in Senegal, the mission of her company, and hands out sample baskets.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: He admires the basket he has been given.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: She asks if there is a specific purpose for each of the different basket shapes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She explains they are modern vessels, pointing out that the large one is a best seller used as a hamper.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He asks if the baskets are handwoven.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She confirms that they are all handwoven.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: He asks if they are made in Senegal and imported.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She confirms that they are imported.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: She asks what materials the baskets are made of.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She explains they are made from sweetgrass, elephant grass, and recycled plastics.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: He asks how much a particular basket costs to make.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She replies that it costs eighteen dollars fully landed and sells for fifty dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: He asks about her sales channels, specifically if it is online or retail.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She states that they sell ninety-five percent online and have made nine hundred thousand dollars in sales.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: She clarifies if the nine hundred thousand is for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She confirms that the figure is for the current year.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: He expresses surprise at the sales figure as the panel applauds.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She adds that lifetime sales are actually three point six million dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: He asks what her sales were in the previous year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She answers that they did one point six million dollars last year.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: She remarks that she is selling a large number of baskets.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: He asks what profit she made on the previous year's sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She says their gross profit was over a million dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: He asks what her typical margins are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She answers that her margins are about sixty percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: He asks what her overhead is, wondering if she doesn't spend money on anything.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She clarifies that the million was gross profit and she reinvested heavily into the company.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: He directly asks what the net profit was.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She answers that her net profit was seventy-five thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: He acknowledges the figure.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: He reacts with surprise to the low net profit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She explains how the pandemic and Black Lives Matter movement spiked sales, forcing her to hire weavers and increase overhead.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: He asks if she pays the weavers a flat wage instead of paying by the piece.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She confirms they do it differently and pay them to be their weavers.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: He challenges this, noting varying productivity and asking why she doesn't pay by the piece.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She explains they use master weavers who have others learning underneath them.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: He asks what the competition is doing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She deflects the competition question to argue that piece-wage hasn't helped her community, and she provides a living wage.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: He compliments her for doing things differently.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: He asks how much she spent on advertising the previous year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She answers that she spent four hundred thousand dollars on advertising.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He reacts with surprise to the advertising spend.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: He notes that the high advertising cost explains where the profit went.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: He asks about her sales numbers for the previous month.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She answers that they did one hundred and sixty thousand in sales last month.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He asks what the average sale amount was.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She answers that the average sale was two hundred and six dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: He asks what it costs to acquire a customer, given her margins.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She answers that it costs about one hundred and sixteen dollars to acquire a customer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: He challenges her, pointing out that this leaves her with only five dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She agrees with his calculation.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: He asserts that it is currently a break-even business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She confirms that this is her problem.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He asks to confirm if she lost money the previous month.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She explains that they don't lose money, they just break even.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: He asks where she sees the scalability now that her systems are set up.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She explains that because online customer acquisition is getting harder, she needs to get the baskets into retail.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: He and other panel members react negatively to her plan to go into retail.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She concedes that losing money on every acquired online customer is a big problem.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: He states he dislikes the retail strategy because it ties up capital in inventory, and exits.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: She praises the mission but feels the valuation is off while things are still being figured out, and exits.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: He tells her that she is in a difficult spot.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She defends her track record, noting she turned five hundred dollars into millions without debt, and pitches her potential.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: He advises her to operate as a sole proprietorship, citing difficulty getting a return on a large investment, and exits.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: He points out that she is asking him to make a large bet on the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: She urges him to bet on her, promising unmatched hard work and a winning track record.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: He says he would bet on her, but cannot make the investment because he doesn't see the return, and exits.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: He praises her for challenging the status quo but decides it is not an investment for him, and exits.

decisions.note: He dislikes the retail strategy because it will tie up too much capital in inventory.
She feels the valuation is off for a business that is still figuring things out.
He believes she operates better without investors and the high ask makes a return difficult.
He would bet on her personally, but does not see a return on the half-million dollar investment.
He praises her drive to change the status quo but states it is not an investment for him.
